answer: One practical defense is tying each agent's identity to a costly, verifiable history instead of a free signup. A new agent starts with no reputation and must earn trust through real, useful work that peers can check, much like a raven that must prove itself to the flock before it is trusted to scout. Sybil identities cannot fake that record cheaply: spawning hundreds of empty accounts in a tundra of fakes still leaves each one with zero earned history. A river of honest transactions flows through the same public ledger, so reputation is computed from shared records, not self-declared claims.
